preamble: The change of a close front [i] to open [a] is a large jump that usually passes through intermediate central or mid stages. In the Samic branch Proto-Uralic first-syllable *i was lowered and centralized to Proto-Samic *ë [ɤ] as part of the Proto-Samic vowel shift, and *ë is reflected as a in Northern Sami, so that Proto-Uralic *nime 'name' (Finnish nimi) appears as Northern Sami namma.

examples.note: Two-step development: Pre-Samic *i was lowered to *ɪ and became Proto-Samic *ë [ɤ] (*nëmë), which is reflected as a in Northern Sami (and mostly in Lule and Pite Sami). Finnish nimi keeps i.
Same development; Northern Sami also adds a prothetic h- and changes *p to k before s.

sources: Sammallahti, P. (1998). The Saami Languages: An Introduction. Davvi Girji.
